why: The edits are spelled out and match the code (change() at actions.ts line 72 guarded by checkPermission 'settings:write' through workMember(), 58 inWorkLang calls in seven files, the five owner views), and owner-pages.test.ts, permissions.scan, the int tests and copies.scan catch most slips. But commit 1 rewraps every Work change action's guard through storeAction() across 58 actions, commit 2 swaps the SQL that sums payments and credit notes behind what owners are told they are owed, and commit 5 leaves the executor to pick which overview sections share markup to get under 800 lines; a slip in any of these can pass the tests.
harm_if_wrong: A Work action that lets a member without settings:write change invoices or clients, or owed and paid figures on the Work overview that are wrong for some invoices, both passing the tests.
make_it_cheaper: Name in commit 5 the exact sections to move (by heading id) instead of 'the sections both files draw with the same markup', so commit 5 drops to cheap and only commits 1 and 2 need a reader.
brief_problems: Commit 5 ends in an open instruction ('move a section into an exported part') tied to a line-count target, which invites cutting until the number fits.
The done_when twin count (16 or less) depends on step 3.13's result, which may not hold when this runs.
